It seems like it's difficult to find a solidly made Warhammer 40000 based game these days but man oh man is this one of the solid ones. 

The dev team clearly did their research into the universe and background of 40K, and most importantly Space Marines. Every weapon sounds and feels powerful and intimidating as they should when held in your power armored mitts. The attention to detail when it comes to the character models and voicing is impressive. 

Overall a very entertaining game to play whether you are a die hard Warhammer fan like myself or just someone who thought it looked like fun buy.

Warhammer 40K: Space Marine is a 3rd shooter that I'd never thought I liked.  Being a Warhammer 40k virgin, this game thrusts me into the impressive lore head first and got me very interested in Warhammer 40K other storylines. The story, characters and gameplay are all well paced, there was no where in the game where I got frustrated or lost (Played in Hard difficulty mind you.) I would recommend this game to any who like shooters and a good story.

The Good: The sheer numbers of Xenos you'll be shooting at is just impressive, Power weapons looks and feel awesome and excellent pacing.

The Bad: If you're used to 3rd Person Shooters like Gears of War, you'll be disappointed.

This game does have some nostalgia with me, so I recently re-played it.

Pro's:
- Amazing sound effects
- Good voices
- Nice effects

Cons:
- Graphics are quite bad, especially up close which happens a lot of time
- Movement is annoying
- Extreamly linear, not nessecarily a bad thing but it's bad here
- Sounds are still there from Servo Skulls even when picked up
- General feel of the game being a cash grab
- No multiplayer anymore :(

Score: 6.5/10. It was amazing when it came out, but has aged badly. Very little replayability, will not recommend.

I bought this game years ago and only put a few hours on it simply because I didn't have any time at the time I purchased it.  So after a recent playthough with fresh eyes I have to say this game is still good. I will compare the good with the bad below.

The Good
 The gameplay is somewhat arcade style shoot em up, and hack and slash... but it is awesome at it, and it does do exactly what you want it to do. The game gives you the perspective of being one of the baddest military soldiers in the universe. One that has waged countless wars in ever ongoing combat and still just thinks it is just another day. The space marine allows you to play as a ranged combat specialist if you so choose, but that is not where I would say the game excels. For you to get the real feel of the rage, the aggressiveness, and brutality that is the satirical world of Warhammer, you have to wade into the melee combat of the game and get your hands dirty with the blood of a thousand Orks. 

Nothing makes you change your perspective on your days playing wow, starcraft, or other warhammer titles like when you stun and ork, then grab him one armed pick him up then body slam him and finally for the finisher step on his head which explodes like watermelon on an old Gallagher comedy night. THAT RIGHT THERE IS HOW YOU KILL AN ORK! I heard myself saying. No other game that I have played gave that absolute sense of well done, as when you make it through a huge onslaught of orks, and finally execute the last one. 

So for pure action, and gameplay fun, I give it a 10/10.

The musical score is epic and fully orchestral so it sounds great, the voice acting is top notch, with major Hollywood actors doing the voiceovers and the game plays perfectly without flaw. 

The Bad

The storyline is good lets say 6/10, and extraordinarily linear almost like a COD game. This is not entirely bad, but you cannot focus on the story to make you want to replay the game since by the 6 or 7th playthough, you can speak the lines yourself. The game features a very consolish style of saving content. You know what I mean, it auto save's every so often and then tells you you will lose progress if you quit playing... and honestly, you will want to keep playing this game, but because it has an 8 hour story or so, you can no life through the content rather quickly, and after playing for 6 or 7 hours straight feel a bit fatigued, not by the game, but by the repetition that a space marine must feel after killing thousands of orks and seeing no end in sight. 

So on that front, I would say the game designers could have given the player a bit more dialog, and even side quest or something to prevent that feeling from becoming prominent. The way I see it, I can play for around 4 or 5 hours, and not feel fatigued, so I should manage my own experience and keep it positive. 

So overall I would recommend this game. It does exactly what it is supposed to do. The small exception that I can see is that you must manage your own expectations and not overdo the game too much or it will become boring or disappointing when it is not the game, it is you.

This game is definitely one of my favorite games out there. The combat is extremely satisfying and gameplay feels quite immersive. Playing as a space marine makes you feel like a true badass. I bought this game on release and now, 6 years later, playing with a friend who just got this game is still fun. It's a worthy buy, on sale or not. I especially recommend being the game though if it is on sale. Enjoy :3

Such a great and fun game! My only complaint it that the campaign is way too short. If youre a big fan of third person shooters, i highly recommend you play this game. Get ready to hear the words "SPACE MARINE!" alot lol!

Some say it's a GoW ripoff, but for WH40k fans that's finally a game that can be played without a feeling of shame. Apart from GW's licensing policy, Space Marine is one of very few examples how bigger budget games in W40k universe can be done. 

Combat is simple, but satisfying - the 'kick' of the bolters and the meaty sound of chainswords - these are things expected from the proper 40k game. It wouldn't hurt if some variation regarding swords was added. 

The only issue I have is the clunkiness of battling enemy SM in the campaign - it just doesn't feel as meaty as shooting or slicing the orks.

Multiplayer was fun, although I'm not a big fan of this mode in any game, so I cannot go deeper in analysing it.

Overall solid 7/10.

Fun action game in the Warhammer 40,000 universe. Decent story. Probably not worth buying the DLC unless you have friend you want to play it with, as there is hardly anyone playing online in most of the DLC modes.

Short, sweet, and bloody good fun.

It's not perfect, there were a few missions where the checkpoint was after the point at which you could chose your weapons and I got stuck with completely the wrong set of weaponry for the set piece but other than that it was very enjoyable if not amazing.

Buy it on sale.

I played two hours of this game and then switched to Soma and Stasis. It's not a bad game, it does quite well portray what it be like to be a SPace Marine and fight a lot of Orks. It's just that it's just that it has nothing going for it beyond being a Space marine and fighting Orks. Buy it on discount if you want to be a Space Marine and fight Orks, but if your looking for anything with more depth or enemies beyond Orks, then go for the Dawn of War series.

Also, there just isn't enough Orks. Seriously, this game needs at least doubel the amount of Orks.

I've recently really got into warhammer 40k, especially the dawn of war titles (I and II), and I very much enjoy this game too. The 3rd person gameplay element is a nice change up in the series considering most of them are rts's or board game like releases. Combat feels fluent and smooth, story is interesting and voice acting is is on par. It does take quite a bit of time for the enemys to vary but apart from that it's a great game.

Fun for a play or two.

Only buy if on sale.

This is by far the greatest non RTS W40k to have been released. The graphics are beautiful, the weapons rock, the combat epic (and loud :P). I know its old but i still hope a sequel or something on its level will be released. The only thing im not a fan of about it is only that the multiplayer isnt really active anymore.

Oh, hell yes!  Purge the Xenos!  This is what being a superhuman killing machine should fel like!  Add in a pretty good, if short, story, and toss in a jump pack with a Storm Hammer, and yeah...you will be smiling like a purging Inquisitor (lunatic) when you're crashing through hordes of orks or...other things!

If you're not aware of the tabletop game, buy this.  If you are familiar with the tabletop, why haven't you bought this yet?
